grand_strategy.reading:
Russia in 2026 runs a grand strategy with one fixed aim - a Ukraine that is not a
state in the Western sense - and a shrinking set of means to reach it. At the
technical and tactical levels the war is being won slowly: Kursk retaken, 0.72% of
Ukraine gained in 2025, Oreshnik over Kyiv. At the level of theatre strategy it has
stalled: the front moves by villages, the price is a budget 40% military, a 21% key
rate and civilian investment in collapse, and the manpower comes from Pyongyang. At
the level of grand strategy the picture inverts, as Luttwak says it must: the move
meant to push NATO back brought Finland and Sweden in and Germany to rearm; the move
meant to free Russia from the West handed its trade, its currency and its machine
tools to China; the levers that hold Belarus pushed Armenia and Azerbaijan away. The
one genuine success since 2025 is diplomatic - the bilateral channel to Washington,
Riyadh to Anchorage to the 28-point plan - and it rests on a paradox too: the demand
for the Donbas is what keeps Trump talking and what keeps any talk from ending. Three
signals that are not rows: Ushakov quietly dropped the 'spirit of Anchorage' slogan
in mid-2026; the New Delhi BRICS declaration dropped Ukraine altogether; and Vucic
stayed away from the 2026 parade while Fico came and did not watch it. The culminating
point of this attrition war is visible from Moscow as from Kyiv; what Moscow has not
yet decided is whether the thaw with Washington is a way to stop before it or a way
to pass it.

stances.note: The one 'adversary' in Russia's Europe, and the structural case the ontology was written for: Moscow's declared aim is not a border but the end of Ukraine as currently constituted - 'one people', 'all of Ukraine is ours' (Putin, June 2025), neutrality, a capped army and a government Moscow can accept (ISW's reading of the Kremlin position, Feb 2026), with 'denazification' never defined. The terms of 14 Jun 2024 (the four oblasts in full, no NATO, recognition, sanctions lifted) were repeated unchanged in Istanbul, Anchorage, Abu Dhabi and Geneva, and the Kremlin suspended trilateral talks until Ukraine leaves the rest of Donetsk. Stable: the aim has not moved while the means (Kursk retaken, Oreshnik on Kyiv) have. Bond - kin, from Moscow's side: the Kremlin's claim of a shared people is the argument for denying the state, which is why Kyiv's own bond is grievance; the pair is deliberately asymmetric in bond and symmetric in grade.
